topic: What happens if you fall from a plane without a parachute?
title: Falling Without A Parachute
idea: After about ten seconds you stop speeding up, and the only clues to surviving come from real cases, not tests.
hook: You fall out of a plane with no parachute.

beats.line: You fall faster every second. Guess your top speed.
beats.see: Character tumbles belly down through clouds; a big speedometer climbs and a '? MPH' guess card pops up. Needle jumps on 'faster', card on 'Guess'.

beats.line: About ten seconds in, the air pushing up matches gravity.
beats.see: Two arrows on the body: a wind arrow from below grows until it equals the gravity arrow from above; the speedometer needle freezes. Arrows equal on 'matches'.

beats.line: Belly down, that's about one hundred twenty miles an hour.
beats.see: Needle locked on 120 with a stamp TOP SPEED; clouds stream past at a steady rate. Stamp on 'twenty'.

beats.line: Honest truth. Nobody has ever tested how to survive this.
beats.see: Freeze frame mid fall; an empty lab clipboard labeled TESTED METHODS with a big zero. Zero on 'Nobody'.

beats.line: Survivor cases point to three things. None is a guarantee.
beats.see: Three case folders slide in, each stamped NO GUARANTEE in red. Folders on 'three', stamp on 'guarantee'.
Step card 1 FEET FIRST; the falling figure rotates upright, feet pointing down. Rotation on 'feet'.

beats.line: Two. Something soft, like snow or trees.
beats.see: Step card 2 SOFT; the ground below swaps from concrete to snow, then to a pine forest. Snow on 'snow', trees on 'trees'.

beats.line: Three. A slope, so the stop takes longer.
beats.see: Step card 3 SLOPE; flat ground tilts into a long hill and a stop timer stretches from short to long. Tilt on 'slope', timer on 'longer'.

beats.line: Vesna Vulović fell thirty three thousand feet, pinned inside a plane's tail.
beats.see: Paper cutout of a broken airliner tail section falling, a small figure trapped inside; altitude counter reads 33,000 FT. Counter on 'thirty', tail on 'tail'.

end.line: The tail hit a snowy slope. She lived. Two out of three.
end.see: The tail slides down a snowy hill and stops; cards 2 SOFT and 3 SLOPE light up with check marks, card 1 stays gray. Slide on 'slope', checks on 'Two'.

description: Fall from a plane with no parachute and you stop speeding up after ten seconds. Then what?

facts.claim: A falling body stops speeding up when air resistance equals weight (terminal velocity), reached after roughly 10 to 12 seconds; belly-down roughly 120 mph.
facts.source: Textbook physics, OpenStax University Physics vol. 1 ch. 6.4 (FACTS file: TO BE RE-CHECKED before render)

facts.claim: There is no tested procedure for surviving a fall without a parachute.
Case reports point to landing feet first, on snow, trees or a slope, which spread the stop over more time.
Vesna Vulović survived a fall of 10,160 m (33,333 ft) on 26 January 1972, pinned inside the tail section, which landed on a snowy slope; Guinness record for highest fall survived without a parachute.

notes: Terminal velocity numbers are marked TO BE RE-CHECKED against OpenStax in the FACTS file; check before render. Script says 'belly down' so head-down speed is not implied. Vulović is clearly inside the tail, not a free body. 'Thirty three thousand feet' rounds 33,333 down. End line 'Two out of three' = snow and slope matched her case, feet first did not apply; it is a callback, not a claim she followed any method. TTS may mispronounce Vulović (voo-LOH-vitch); consider a phonetic override. Big number: about one hundred twenty miles an hour.
